item.title: Sheriff Whittle is phasing out dash cams, even as critics renew call for body cameras
item.description: The Columbia County Sheriff’s Office is slowly ending the use of dash cameras in patrol cars. Sheriff Clay Whittle says the cameras cost too much, wear out quickly and have been replaced by newer tools. The post Sheriff Whittle is phasing out dash cams, even as critics renew call for body cameras appeared first on The Augusta Press.

item.title: Error in state auditors’ data center review inflated job production and economic value
item.description: Data centers in Georgia did not produce the same high payback in exchange for nearly half a billion dollars in tax breaks as reported by state auditors last month, according to a correction issued Wednesday. The post Error in state auditors’ data center review inflated job production and economic value appeared first on The Augusta Press.

item.description: Gov. Brian Kemp’s last budget proposal would stockpile billions for any rough economy one of his successors might encounter while also asking lawmakers to return over $1 billion to taxpayers. item.description: As Georgia’s 12th Congressional District heads toward the 2026 election, a growing field of candidates including five Democrats and one Republican is lining up to unseat Rep. item.title: Columbia County Planning Commission votes to recommend approval for all three rezoning requests for data center development
item.description: The Columbia County Planning Commission has voted to recommend approval for all three of the controversial rezoning requests in the county’s District 4, all to make way for proposed data center developments.
